records.title: Show HN: Airweave – Let agents search any app
records.author: lennertjansen
records.storyText:
Hey HN, we're Lennert and Rauf. We’re building Airweave (https://github.com/airweave-ai/airweave), an open-source tool that lets agents search and retrieve data from any app or database. Here’s a general intro: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EFI-7SYGQ48, and here’s a longer one that shows more real-world use cases, examples of how Airweave is used by Cursor (0:33) and Claude desktop (2:04), etc.: https://youtu.be/p2dl-39HwQo

A couple of months ago we were building agents that interacted with different apps and were frustrated when they struggled to handle vague natural language requests like "resolve that one Linear issue about missing auth configs", "if you get an email from an unsatisfied customer, reimburse their payment in Stripe", or "what were the returns for Q1 based on the financials sheet in gdrive?", only to have the agent inefficiently chain together loads of function calls to find the data or not find it at all and hallucinate.

We also noticed that despite the rise of MCP creating more desire for agents to interact with external resources, the majority of agent dev tooling focused on function calling and actions instead of search. We were annoyed by the lack of tooling that enabled agents to semantically search workspace or database contents, so we started building Airweave first as an internal solution. Then we decided to open-source it and pursue it full time after we got positive reactions from coworkers and other agent builders.

Airweave connects to productivity tools, databases, or document stores via their APIs and transforms their contents into searchable knowledge bases, accessible through a standardized interface for the agent. The search interface is exposed via REST or MCP. When using MCP, Airweave essentially builds a semantically searchable MCP server on top of the resource. The platform handles the entire data pipeline from connection and extraction to chunking, embedding, and serving. To ensure knowledge is current, it has automated sync capabilities, with configurable schedules and change detection through content hashing.

We built it with support for white-labeled multi-tenancy to provide OAuth2-based integration across multiple user accounts while maintaining privacy and security boundaries. We're also actively working on permission-awareness (i.e., RBAC on the data) for the platform.

So happy to share learnings and get insights from your experiences. looking forward to comments!

records.title: Show HN: CLI that spots fake GitHub stars, risky dependencies and licence traps
records.author: artski
records.storyText:
When I came across a study that traced 4.5 million fake GitHub stars, it confirmed a suspicion I’d had for a while: stars are noisy. The issue is they’re visible, they’re persuasive, and they still shape hiring decisions, VC term sheets, and dependency choices—but they say very little about actual quality.

I wrote StarGuard to put that number in perspective based on my own methodology inspired with what they did and to fold a broader supply-chain check into one command-line run.

It starts with the simplest raw input: every starred_at timestamp GitHub will give. It applies a median-absolute-deviation test to locate sudden bursts. For each spike, StarGuard pulls a random sample of the accounts behind it and asks: how old is the user? Any followers? Any contribution history? Still using the default avatar? From that, it computes a Fake Star Index, between 0 (organic) and 1 (fully synthetic).

But inflated stars are just one issue. In parallel, StarGuard parses dependency manifests or SBOMs and flags common risk signs: unpinned versions, direct Git URLs, lookalike package names. It also scans licences—AGPL sneaking into a repo claiming MIT, or other inconsistencies that can turn into compliance headaches.

It checks contributor patterns too. If 90% of commits come from one person who hasn’t pushed in months, that’s flagged. It skims for obvious code red flags: eval calls, minified blobs, sketchy install scripts—because sometimes the problem is hiding in plain sight.

All of this feeds into a weighted scoring model. The final Trust Score (0–100) reflects repo health at a glance, with direct penalties for fake-star behaviour, so a pretty README badge can’t hide inorganic hype.

I added for the fun of it it generating a cool little badge for the trust score lol.

Under the hood, its all uses, heuristics, and a lot of GitHub API paging. Run it on any public repo with:

python starguard.py owner/repo --format markdown It works without a token, but you’ll hit rate limits sooner.

Please provide any feedback you can.

records.title: Show HN: Git-Native Client (free, no login)
records.author: nikolasdimi
records.storyText:
Hey HN,

We recently started working on a tool called Voiden and wanted to share it here to get your thoughts and feedback.

Over the years, we found ourselves managing way too many tools just to work with APIs: one for api specs, another for docs, a third for tests, etc etc. Eventually it starts to feel more like a performance than actual work.

So we built Voiden: A git-native, extensible, and lightweight client that brings everything—specs, docs, tests, mocks—into one place. No bloat, no lock-in, no "platform overhead." Just structured API workflows that don’t fight your tools or your team.

A few things we care about:

-Reusability and composability : APIs as building blocks, not silos.

-Structure over scatter : everything lives together in one workspace.

-No sign-in required : you can use it without creating an account.

Free and open — we are building this with the community in mind.

Just to be clear: The goal is NOT to replace OpenAPI, but to provide a layer around existing specs that feels coherent, hackable, and friendly to real-world dev workflows.

You can check it out here: https://voiden.md/

And if you have feedback, suggestions, or just want to follow along:

https://github.com/VoidenHQ/feedback

We are still early, but would love to hear what you think—what you like, what is missing. Appreciate any time you take to try it out.

Nikolas

records.title: Show HN: Grapple, a DIY data platform that uses AI the Right Way
records.author: andrewicarlson
records.storyText:
Hello again, HN! My name is Andrew, and my cofounder Jack (@jackonawalk) and I are excited to show off a project years in the making – a data platform where the only prerequisite is data.

Most "self-service" data tools aren't really self-service. They assume you've already set up a data warehouse, configured pipelines, defined semantic data models, and usually, the best escape hatch is to explore the underlying data warehouse yourself. That's an intimidating proposition for most people who don't consider themselves data experts.

Grapple abstracts the data architecture and ships with everything you need to start working with the data you already have. It comes with a data warehouse, an ETL for connecting data from existing sources, semantic data models, and a visualization layer to build dashboards and reporting. All you need to bring is your data.

Oh, and the AI thing? We're bullish on safe, secure, and governable use of AI. We use a LLM to help generate calculations and formulas, but it never has access to the underlying data, only the schema. Everything the LLM generates is auditable and editable by the user. We believe this is the most secure way to get the benefits of a LLM while preserving absolute data integrity – no hallucinated data!

You can try it out with just a CSV upload. No credit card or sensitive data required. There's a demo video on our homepage and a gallery of public dashboards here: https://cloudgrapple.com/gallery

Let us know what you think!

records.title: Show HN: MCP Browser Agent – Autonomous Browser Automation for Claude Desktop
records.author: ivanimprv
records.storyText:
Hey HN! Following up on MCPs for Claude, I've created another Model Context Protocol server that gives Claude Desktop autonomous browser automation capabilities.

The Browser Agent MCP lets Claude control a headful browser to navigate websites, capture screenshots, manipulate DOM elements, execute JavaScript, and perform API requests—all through natural language instructions.

Check out a demo here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0lMsKiTy7TE Repository: https://github.com/imprvhub/mcp-browser-agent

With this MCP integration, you can: - Navigate to any URL with configurable load strategies - Capture full-page or element-specific screenshots - Perform precise DOM interactions (click, fill, select, hover) - Execute arbitrary JavaScript with console logs capture - Make HTTP requests (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) with headers and body

What makes this a true AI agent is its persistent browser session. Claude maintains state across multiple commands, captures console logs, stores screenshots as resources, and can chain operations for complex workflows.

It's particularly useful for web testing, form automation, data extraction, or creating visual documentation. The setup requires Node.js, Claude Desktop, and Playwright dependencies. The browser runs headful by default with chrome (you can change to firefox, chromium and more).

If you've been exploring MCP development or browser automation, I'd love to hear about your use cases. What other browser capabilities would enhance your AI Agents workflows?

The project is open source under Mozilla Public License 2.0, and I welcome contributions if you're interested in MCP development or want to extend the automation features.

records.title: Show HN: I wrote 111 short stories about the future –free on Kindle for few days
records.author: animadellafesta
records.storyText:
Hi HN,

I’m a 51-year-old freelance programmer from Italy. Between projects (and rants about modern web design), I ended up writing 111 short stories imagining what the future might look like — sometimes weird, sometimes funny, sometimes a bit too real.

Themes range from AI governments and post-capitalist ruins to synthetic emotions, invisible wars, and dystopian customer service. It’s called Chronicles from the Future — speculative fiction in fast, sharp doses. Some stories are just a paragraph, others take a few minutes. The whole thing was first published in Italian; I just translated it into English myself.

The Kindle version is free this week on Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0F7ZRX1BN

If you check it out, I’d love to know what you think. Even just which title made you curious.

Thanks for reading — and for tolerating a non-startup post.

records.title: Show HN: Startup Marketing Case Studies
records.author: elananandhan
records.storyText:
I'm Elan, a SaaS marketer with 15+ years of experience. I've led marketing for two SaaS products from zero to $1M in revenue.

I recently launched a newsletter called Startup Marketing. Every other week, I break down the marketing strategies behind B2B startups that grew from $0 to $1M.

There are plenty of SaaS growth deep dives out there—but most try to cover everything: product, sales, and marketing. As a result, the marketing insights often feel surface-level.

So I focus only on the marketing side—what they did, how they did it, and why it worked. I've published 8 case studies so far, with the next one dropping this week.

Would love your feedback—and ideas for making it better.

records.title: Show HN: Chrome Tool to Compare Top Investors Portfolios for Common Holdings
records.author: Thilak_Thakur
records.storyText:
Hello HN,

I made Superstar Investors Tracker : chrome extension to discover common stocks among top Investors portfolios. Since a year, I've been contemplating building a tool to discover common stocks in top investors' portfolios.Now, amidst my job hunting, I finally had the opportunity to bring this idea to life. As an active investor in the stock market since 2019, I've found value in analyzing and investing in the portfolios of renowned investors. I observed, identifying overlapping stock holdings among these investors can provide insights into high-conviction investments. However, manually comparing extensive portfolios—Buffett's 40 holdings, Dalio's 691, and Kenneth C. Griffin's over 3,800 and more..—is both time-consuming ,prone to errors and practically impossible as list grows.This challenge inspired me to create a tool that automates the process. Finally sample screenshot of how output looks like : https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TDq3W6vdJURCbkh3R-l10nnMMkX...

Key Features:

Scrape and compare portfolios from Top investors of your choice.

Automatically identify common stock holdings.

Display a list of investors associated with each overlapping stock.

Export results to CSV or XLSX for further analysis.

Responsive UI designed for clarity and speed.

No login required.

Free to use.

The extension is built using plain JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, utilizing Chrome's storage capabilities to scrape static webpages—no third-party APIs involved.

Not all websites display portfolios of Top Investors until we pay premium and some websites allow but each website is unique in itself. So I've presently listed some websites with their links in the FAQ section of the official site. Currently, the extension is tailored for Indian and U.S. investors. To see the extension in action, there is a short demo video in official website.

I'd love to hear your feedback and suggestions!

records.title: Show HN: HLExport–Export Apple Health data to JSON in one tap (offline)
records.author: orenodinner
records.storyText:
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hlexport/id6745495959

*Problem* Apple Health on iPhone locks raw data behind an XML export that’s 100 MB+ and painful to parse. I wanted a programmatic, privacy-friendly way to feed that data into notebooks and LLMs.

*Solution* HLExport (SwiftUI): * Reads every HealthKit type between any start/end date * Outputs compact JSON (share sheet or clipboard) * 7-level mood logger (`HKCategoryTypeIdentifier.stateOfMind`) * All on-device; no backend; MIT-licensed

Under 600 KB binary size. iOS 17+ (mood write: iOS 18). Happy to answer questions & take suggestions – this is weekend-project code that I’d like to harden with your feedback.

records.title: Show HN: I’m building a tool to unify job tracking, skills, and salary insights
records.author: BluBeeAI
records.storyText:
After 20 years of navigating different roles in tech and business, I kept running into the same problem: managing a career meant stitching together job boards, resumes, spreadsheets, salary tools, and vague advice. It felt like a mess of disconnected parts with no system to it.
So, I started building BluBee.ai — a career management platform that tries to unify all of that, with a little help from AI. It’s still early, but here’s what I’m working on:
• Unified Dashboard: Track job applications, skill gaps, and goals in one place
• AI Suggestions: Career moves based on your experience and interests
• Market Insights: Salary trends, in-demand skills, and company-level data
• Portfolio Builder: A way to present your work that’s more than just a PDF
• Mobile-Friendly: Clean design, works well on the go, dark/light modes included
It’s very much a work in progress, and I’m learning a lot as I go — especially around how much people don’t trust black-box AI when it comes to career advice.
I’d love feedback, especially from folks who’ve tried building tools like this or rolled their own systems out of frustration. What have you hacked together for your own career management? What’s broken that no one seems to be fixing?

records.title: Show HN: A Human-Centered Protocol for Containment-Aware AI Design
records.author: architect137
records.storyText:
I’ve written a small protocol for engineers and researchers working on advanced AI systems LLMs, agents, simulators, where alignment can’t be assumed.

It’s called the "AI Human Protection Protocol". It’s not a manifesto or policy paper. It’s a design-layer spec focused on recursive coherence, boundary maintenance, and preserving human agency as systems scale.

I've done some evaluation against common symbolic failure patterns, including recursive collapse scenarios like Roko’s Basilisk, Surveillance Capitalism, Technocracy, Synthetic Gods, Simulated Suffering (Hellbox), 2001: A Space Odyssey, The Matrix... all the classics.

It’s meant as a practical foundation for containment-aware system design, simple enough to implement, general enough to extend.

If you’re working in the space and want to help pressure-test or improve it, I’d appreciate feedback. Especially from folks who’ve thought deeply about recursion, autonomy, or edge-case behaviour in aligned systems.

Protocol: https://github.com/fieldarchitect137/AI-Human-Protection-Pro...

Core breach pattern reference: https://github.com/fieldarchitect137/AI-Human-Protection-Pro...

records.title: Show HN: Browser-based screen recorder (for bug reporting)
records.author: rikroots
records.storyText:
The main use case for the product is bug reporting. When a user encounters an issue with a website (or other product) they can navigate to this web page and screen capture the issue in a more meaningful way to help product developers identify and fix the problem.

tl;dr: It Works On My Machine (specifically Chrome running on MacBook Pro M2). There needs to be a lot more work done to get the page working on desktop Firefox/Safari browsers. Support to get the page working on mobile browsers is out-of-scope for this side project.

Also tl;dr: Built in vanilla HTML, CSS and Javascript. No frameworks. No toolchains or build steps. All functionality is client-side: no sign-in or registration required. No added tracking. Page can be self hosted and/or downloaded and run locally. YMMV. Enjoy!

records.title: Show HN: I built a system to make ChatGPT brutally honest with you

-----

If you’re serious about using ChatGPT to grow and

records.title: Show HN: All-in-one platform for your equity research
records.author: freeJeffery
records.storyText:
Hi,

Over the past year, I’ve been building Palmy, a modern equity research platform designed to empower investors with deep, data-rich insights. Some major features are:

Palmy is an investment in yourself—built to accelerate your equity research and portfolio management. It’s a fast, accurate, and purpose-built platform for value-focused, data-driven, long-term investors, with:

Global Coverage 15,000 equities, where over 6,000 are operating in the United States.

Financial Statements Explore up to 40 years of annual and quarterly income statements, balance sheets, cash flow reports, and financial ratios. Whether you're conducting deep value research or focusing on dividend plays, Palmy provides the full historical context and metrics to support your strategy.

Wall Street Estimates Stay aligned with market expectations by reviewing historical data alongside forward-looking earnings forecasts.

AI Earnings Reports Digest earnings calls in minutes with AI-generated summaries. Get sharp insights into key metrics, wins and setbacks, competitor mentions, and grouped thematic highlights.

Calendars Track dividends, earnings, and economic events—all neatly organized by date for intuitive navigation.

Workspaces Simplify your investor relations workflow with structured, searchable access to 10-Ks, 10-Qs, proxy statements, and more. Features like auto-indexing, note-taking, and PDF export streamline your research process.

Company Screeners Use powerful screeners—ready-made or custom-built with 250+ financial metrics. Filter by country, sector, or industry to pinpoint the companies that fit your thesis.

Watchlists Organize and monitor investment ideas in dynamic watchlists, complete with relevant news, event alerts, and allocation insights.

Portfolios Track your positions and evaluate performance using visual tools and essential metrics like Alpha (α), Beta (β), and the Sharpe Ratio.

Please let me know what you think of my platform :) Do you use alternatives? Would be happy to discuss about your research workflows.
